name: Kohath
overview: Kohath was a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as a son of Levi. He is listed among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, marking him as an important ancestral figure within the Levitical lineage. His descendants, the Kohathites, are noted in the biblical census records, emphasizing his role as a progenitor of a significant Levitical clan.
namesAndTitles: The name Kohath appears as a proper name in Scripture without an explicit meaning or divine origin provided. It is simply recorded as the name of this Levitical ancestor in Genesis 46:11.
familyAndRelationships: Kohath is explicitly identified as a son of Levi. Inferred relationships include his fatherhood of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, as well as a brotherly connection to Jochebed. Additionally, he is an ancestor to notable descendants such as Azariah, Zechariah, and Meshullam, indicating his foundational place within the Levitical family line.
scriptureSignificance: Kohath is significant in the biblical narrative as the progenitor of the Kohathite clan, one of the key Levitical families entrusted with sacred duties in Israel. His inclusion among the sons of Israel who migrated to Egypt situates him at a pivotal moment in Israel's history, linking the patriarchal period to the Exodus era. Through his descendants, Kohath's lineage contributed to the religious leadership and worship practices that foreshadow Christ's priestly ministry.
